bud borer.description: A destructive pest infestation where caterpillar larvae bore into tender flower buds, inflorescence, and growing tips of the arecanut palm, severely reducing crop yield.
bud borer.cause: Larvae of the moth Tirathaba rufivena, which feed on tender plant parts.
symptoms: Small bore holes on inflorescence and buttons.
Accumulation of fine frass (fecal matter) and web-like threads near bud bases.
Shedding of tender buttons and blackening of flowers.
Drying and yellowing of surrounding shoots.

treatment.organic_control: Spray Neem Oil (1-3% concentration) or apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) formulations near the crown.
treatment.chemical_control: Apply granular insecticide such as Phorate 10G (10g per palm) to the leaf axils, or spray Chlorpyriphos 20 EC (2 ml/liter) on inflorescences.

preventive_measures: Clean leaf crowns regularly to remove debris.
Install light traps in the plantation to monitor and capture adult moths.
Prune and destroy severely infested inflorescences immediately.

healthy_foot.description: The base and root zone of the palm are clean, sturdy, and free of any fungal rot or physical deformities. This is the optimal baseline state.
healthy_foot.cause: Excellent plantation management, proper drainage, and soil hygiene.
symptoms: Firm, sound bark at the collar region.
Healthy root network visible near the soil surface without decay.
Absence of waterlogging or soft rot.

treatment.organic_control: Apply organic manure and compost annually to maintain soil nutrition.

preventive_measures: Ensure proper sub-surface drainage to prevent water stagnation.
Avoid wounding the collar region during weeding operations.

Healthy_Leaf.description: Foliage exhibits rich green coloring and uniform texture. Photosynthesis is optimal, indicating a healthy palm.
Healthy_Leaf.cause: Balanced nutrient uptake and absence of leaf pathogens or sap-sucking vectors.
symptoms: Dark green, symmetrical leaflets.
No spotting, yellowing, or leaf drying.
Flexible, healthy fronds.

treatment.organic_control: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potash compost levels.

preventive_measures: Apply recommended doses of NPK fertilizers.
Provide micro-irrigation during dry summer months.

Healthy_Nut.description: Areca fruits are developing normally, displaying uniform size, smooth surfaces, and a healthy green-to-orange skin tone.
Healthy_Nut.cause: Balanced trace mineral uptake and optimal water availability.
symptoms: Smooth rind with no blotches or cracks.
Heavy, dense bunches with high button retention.
No signs of rot or insect entry.

treatment.organic_control: Apply organic mulch around the root zone to conserve soil moisture.

preventive_measures: Apply potassium-rich organic manure during the flowering phase.
Maintain a regular irrigation cycle to avoid fruit stress.

Healthy_Trunk.description: The trunk is straight, uniform, and structurally solid without fissures, cracking, or bleeding spots.
Healthy_Trunk.cause: Uniform growth conditions and protection from severe direct sun exposure.
symptoms: Smooth trunk surface with clear leaf scars.
No bleeding or sap exudation.
No vertical structural fissures.
preventive_measures: Shade the trunks of young palms to protect them from sun scorch.
Avoid making cuts or wounds on the trunk during harvesting.

Mahali_Koleroga.description: A highly destructive fungal disease active during heavy monsoons, causing massive shedding of immature nuts and crown rot if left unchecked.
Mahali_Koleroga.cause: Fungal pathogen Phytophthora palmivora, favored by continuous rain, high relative humidity, and cold temperatures.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on the green nuts starting at the calyx.
Massive shedding of green, immature nuts.
White felt-like fungal growth on the fallen nuts.
Rotting of kernel tissues and characteristic foul smell.

treatment.organic_control: Apply bio-control agents like Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens mixed with neem cake to the soil base.
treatment.chemical_control: Prophylactic spraying of 1% Bordeaux mixture before monsoon and again 40 days later. For active outbreaks, spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2g/liter).

preventive_measures: Collect and burn all fallen, diseased nuts to reduce soil spore load.
Ensure proper spacing between palms and thin out overlapping canopies to improve airflow.
Improve drainage to prevent stagnant water around palm feet.

stem cracking.description: A non-pathogenic physiological disorder causing long, vertical structural cracks on the trunks, which exposes the inner fibers to secondary infections.
stem cracking.cause: Sudden fluctuations in soil moisture (dry spells followed by heavy watering) combined with direct hot sun exposure (sun scorch).
symptoms: Long vertical splits/fissures on the trunk, usually on the south-western side.
Fibrous inner tissues exposed to weather.
Gradual narrowing of the crown above the cracked trunk segment.

treatment.organic_control: Apply thick organic mulch (dry leaves, coir pith) around the base to keep soil moisture levels stable.
treatment.chemical_control: Swab/paint the interior of the cracks with Bordeaux paste (10%) to prevent entry of wood-decaying fungi.

preventive_measures: Protect young palm trunks by white-washing them with lime (slaked lime) up to 2 meters high.
Wrap south-western side of trunks with dry areca leaves or thatch material.
Maintain a uniform drip irrigation schedule during summer months to avoid soil drying.

Stem_bleeding.description: A serious fungal disease that attacks the trunk tissues, leading to discoloration, bleeding of dark sap, and internal decay of the palm wood.
Stem_bleeding.cause: Fungal infection Thielaviopsis paradoxa, typically entering through cracks or physical wounds under wet soil conditions.
symptoms: Exudation of a dark, reddish-brown fluid from cracks on the lower trunk.
Blackening and softening of the trunk tissue around the bleeding points.
Hollowing or rot of inner wood upon cutting.
Yellowing and reduction in size of the leaf crown.

treatment.organic_control: Apply Trichoderma viride-enriched organic manures around the basin. Pour Neem cake extract into the root zone.
treatment.chemical_control: Chisel out the infected bark tissue and paint the wound with Bordeaux paste or Tridemorph (Calixin) 5%.

preventive_measures: Avoid waterlogging at all costs by digging deep drainage channels.
Do not prune leaves too close to the stem or slash bark during field tasks.
White-wash the stem base to reflect sun rays and avoid heat cracks.

yellow leaf disease.description: An incurable phytoplasmal disease affecting the vascular system of the palm. It leads to progressive leaf yellowing, root decay, and ultimate death of the palm.
yellow leaf disease.cause: Phytoplasma bacteria, which are transmitted from palm to palm by vector insects like the plant hopper Proutista moesta.
symptoms: Yellowing of inner leaflets, starting from the tips of lower leaves.
Leaflets become narrow, brittle, and crowded in the crown.
Areca nuts in affected palms turn dark, fibrous, and kernel gets decayed.
Rotting of roots and gradual drying of the entire leaf crown.

treatment.organic_control: Apply botanical insecticides such as neem-based sprays to suppress the plant hopper vectors.
treatment.chemical_control: No cure exists for the phytoplasma itself. Control the vectors by spraying Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 ml/liter) or applying systemic Phorate to leaf bases.
treatment.recommended_pesticide: Imidacloprid or Phorate (to control insect vectors)

preventive_measures: Uproot and completely burn severely infected palms to prevent spread to adjacent healthy palms.
Apply high doses of potassium (potash) fertilizer and organic compost to boost palm tolerance.
Plant YLD-resistant areca palm varieties if available in your zone.

Arecanut_YellowBrownSpot.description: Fungal leaf spot disease characterized by distinct yellowish-brown necrotic spots with dark halos on Areca palm fronds.
Arecanut_YellowBrownSpot.cause: Fungal pathogens Colletotrichum gloeosporioides or Helminthosporium species, triggered by warm humid microclimates.
symptoms: Small circular to irregular yellow spots appearing on tender leaflets.
Spot centers turn dark brown or greyish with dark reddish-brown borders.
Coalescence of spots leading to blighting and premature drying of leaflets.

treatment.organic_control: Spray Neem oil 3% or Pseudomonas fluorescens (20g/liter) at 15-day intervals.
treatment.chemical_control: Foliar spray of Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/liter) or Carbendazim 50 WP (1 g/liter).

preventive_measures: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation that keeps leaves wet for prolonged periods.
Maintain adequate spacing between palms to ensure good canopy ventilation.
Remove and burn fallen infected fronds.

CCI_Caterpillars.scientific_name: Slug Caterpillar / Leaf Eating Caterpillar Complex
CCI_Caterpillars.description: Defoliating insect infestation where larvae feed voraciously on Areca leaflets, leaving behind skeletonized fronds.
CCI_Caterpillars.cause: Larvae of Limacodid moths and leaf-eating caterpillars feeding on leaf lamina.
symptoms: Large irregular bite holes along leaflet margins.
Skeletonization of leaf fronds leaving only midribs intact.
Presence of caterpillar larvae and fecal pellets on lower leaf surfaces.

treatment.organic_control: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) at 2g/liter or Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
treatment.chemical_control: Spray Quinalphos 25 EC (2 ml/liter) or Lambda-cyhalothrin 5 EC (1 ml/liter).

preventive_measures: Hand-pick and destroy egg masses and young larval clusters.
Install light traps in orchards to catch adult moths before egg laying.
Encourage natural predators like reduviid bugs and parasitic wasps.

WCLWD_DryingofLeaflets.description: Advanced phase of leaf wilt disease where leaflets undergo severe necrosis, drying from tips inward, leading to reduced frond count.
WCLWD_DryingofLeaflets.cause: Root system decay and vascular blockage associated with phytoplasmal infection and root rot complexes.
symptoms: Necrotic brown drying progressing from leaflet tips toward the rachis.
Brittle, papery texture of affected foliage.
Stunted crown size and poor nut setting.

treatment.organic_control: Apply Trichoderma harzianum enriched neem cake (5 kg/palm/year) to root zone.
treatment.chemical_control: Drench root zone with Copper Oxychloride (3 g/liter) and spray micro-nutrients.

preventive_measures: Ditch deep trenches around infected blocks to isolate root systems.
Apply balanced NPK fertilizer with magnesium sulphate and zinc sulphate.
Eliminate sucking insect vectors from palm crowns.

WCLWD_Flaccidity.description: Intermediate phase of leaf wilt disease characterized by drooping, flaccid leaflets that lose structural turgor pressure.
WCLWD_Flaccidity.cause: Vascular water transport disruption caused by root crown infection.
symptoms: Downward bending and flaccidity of outer leaflets.
Ribbon-like curving of fronds.
Pale green to yellowish discoloration of canopy.

treatment.organic_control: Drench root basin with VAM (Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza) and bio-fertilizers.
treatment.chemical_control: Apply micro-nutrient mixture (Boron, Zinc, Iron) and systemic fungicide.

preventive_measures: Ensure summer irrigation to relieve water stress.
Maintain organic mulch around palm basins.
Regularly inspect palms for early flaccidity signs.

WCLWD_Yellowing.description: Early-stage leaf wilt manifestation featuring golden-yellow chlorosis across middle and lower leaf fronds.
WCLWD_Yellowing.cause: Chlorophyll breakdown due to root damage and vector-transmitted wilt agents.
symptoms: Bright yellowing of inner leaflets starting from lower whorls.
Green veins remaining briefly before full chlorosis.
Reduction in crown vigor and nut yield.

treatment.organic_control: Basal application of neem cake and bio-pesticides.
treatment.chemical_control: Foliar spray of magnesium sulphate (10 g/liter) + micronutrients.

preventive_measures: Boost soil organic carbon with farmyard manure.
Control sap-sucking insect vectors promptly.
Avoid root injuries during inter-cultivation.
